A1.justification: Both PDFs describe the same RLER study. Their text, equations, figures, tables, and complete appendices are readable, and retained content can be matched across the changed title, layout, and appendix numbering.

before.justification: v1 reports original controlled arithmetic experiments, mathematical reasoning benchmark results, component ablations, and unlabeled-data scaling experiments.

after.justification: v2 retains original experiments and adds cross-model and non-mathematical evaluations, sensitivity studies, diversity measurements, and reward-error interventions.

M1.justification: The ensemble, GRPO, selection, and TIES-merging pipeline remains. However, Section 4.2 changes interpolation from (1-alpha)r_H + alpha r_S to (1-alpha)r_S + alpha r_H, retaining the confidence-based alpha definition; Algorithm 1 confirms the reversal. This is a localized but substantive reward-rule revision. The PDFs do not establish whether it corrects the description or changes the implementation.

E1.justification: v2 adds WebInstruct-verified training and MMLU-Pro evaluation across 14 disciplines, substantially extending the tested coverage beyond arithmetic and competition mathematics. Big-Math was already used for data scaling in v1, so its appearance in a dedicated v2 experiment is not itself a newly introduced dataset.

E2.justification: Table 1 adds evaluated INTUITOR and Co-rewarding comparisons alongside the retained Judge, Self-Consistency, and Frequency baselines. The Qwen arithmetic comparison also adds INTUITOR. These stronger comparators materially expand the comparison set and change the best main-task RLIR baseline from 33.0 to 35.3 Avg@8.

E3.justification: The main Qwen2.5-Math-7B configuration remains, but v2 introduces Llama-3.2-3B, Llama-3.1-8B, and Qwen2.5-7B-Instruct evaluations, verifier-based non-math training, and MMLU-Pro Pass@1 reporting. New protocols include temperature and calibration-bound sweeps, fixed versus adaptive interpolation, and ensemble-size comparisons under fixed 16-rollout and increased 32-rollout budgets, with additional diversity and resource metrics.

E4.justification: Beyond the retained component ablations and decoupling studies, Appendix B adds a random-reward control, direct oracle correction of SC false positives and false negatives, temperature and interpolation-bound sensitivity, fixed-weight interpolation controls, diversity evolution, and ensemble accuracy/resource tradeoffs. These investigate additional mechanisms and robustness questions rather than merely adding benchmark scores.

E5.justification: Table 8 newly reports checkpoint accuracy variance and specifies a window of ±5 checkpoints around the best checkpoint. This adds an explicit training-variability statistic. Neither version reports independent training-run counts, seed-based uncertainty estimates, or confidence intervals.

E6.justification: The retained Table 1 numerical entries are unchanged, including RLER's 37.5 Avg@8 and 52.8 Pass@8. v2 adds substantial baseline, cross-model, non-math, sensitivity, diversity, resource, and intervention results. For example, Table 7 reports MMLU-Pro Pass@1 of 55.12 for RLER and 54.82 for Co-rewarding. These are newly reported results, not an improvement in the retained headline RLER score.

T1.justification: The hard-versus-soft reward proof is retained, moving from Appendix A to Appendix C. Limited mathematical changes include removing Section 4.1's explicit convexity-based ensemble-margin inequality and introducing the relative compute proxy in Equation 15, with an assumed backward/forward FLOPs ratio. There is no substantial new theorem or proof.

C1.justification: The central bias diagnosis and RLER contribution remain. The abstract and introduction revise the claimed improvement over the best RLIR baseline from 13.6% to 6.2%, reflecting the stronger comparator rather than lower RLER performance. v2 also explicitly broadens its validation claim across model families and non-mathematical tasks.

C2.justification: The original interpretation of coupling and over-reward remains. v2 adds substantive qualifications about requiring reliable semantic verification beyond mathematics, explains diversity emerging from identical initializations, and discusses diminishing ensemble benefits when per-policy rollout counts shrink while memory grows. These refine applicability and practical tradeoffs without replacing the central explanation.

D1.justification: v2 adds Algorithm 1, defines confidence bounds through quantiles with defaults 0.20 and 0.60, specifies per-policy selection quota caps, discloses common ensemble initialization, and documents rollout/resource accounting. These substantially expand implementation and reproducibility information. The existing prompt is retained in Appendix D rather than newly introduced.

R1.justification: v2 adds references for Llama, General-Reasoner/WebInstruct, and MMLU-Pro, and refines positioning relative to agreement-based, confidence-based, and lagged-policy reward methods. Co-reward's changed bibliographic title corresponds to the same previously cited work. The related-work framework is refined rather than substantially expanded.

P1.justification: The title, abstract, introduction, related work, and substantial portions of the method and results discussion are rewritten around the self-confirming-loop narrative. Explanations and terminology are extensively revised. The appendices are reorganized into an algorithmic workflow, expanded experimental sections, the retained proof, and the retained prompt.

P2.justification: The main text changes from a single-column layout to a two-column conference format, with figures resized and relocated, panel labels added, and captions expanded. The selection table formerly embedded in Figure 6 becomes Table 2. New experimental tables, Figures 8–9, and Algorithm 1 substantially expand the visual presentation; the original plot data are retained.

improvement.justification: Stronger evaluated baselines, additional backbones, broader task coverage, and targeted robustness/resource analyses substantially address v1's limited validation; pseudocode and explicit defaults also improve reproducibility. These gains outweigh reporting problems: the interpolation reversal is unexplained, Appendix B.1.1 retains a 14.1-point arithmetic gain although Table 3 implies 11.1 over INTUITOR, and Figure 9's 70% FP/0% FN panel conflicts with the described FP-only intervention. These issues qualify specific conclusions but do not negate the substantial overall improvement in empirical support.
